rationale:
ROUND 8 of 7ba5b8c4 — every objection answered by MEASUREMENT. No new mechanism.

ROUND 7 WAS 8 APPROVE / 2 OBJECT (reuse_agent, guidelines, tooling_provenance, diagnosis_guardian, compliance, constitution, mission, prior_art_librarian approved; guardian and debug_historian objected; 1 seat unreadable). That is the best round of the eight and the shape changed: **not one objection said the plan is wrong.** All six said the same thing in six voices — *you asserted this; go measure it and cite it.* Severities: two medium, four low. No HIGH.

So round 8 changes NO code, NO globs, NO schema, and adds NO helper. The six edits are byte-identical in substance to round 7. What changed is that six asserted claims are now query results in grounded_in, and one verification step the plan genuinely lacked is added to the VERIFY file. **This is deliberate and it is the lesson of rounds 4-6:** that sequence died because each objection was answered by adding mechanism, and each new mechanism became fresh surface to object to. An objection asking for EVIDENCE must be answered with evidence, never with code. If round 8 does not converge, the conclusion is about the plan, not about an accretion.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, one per objection:

(1) reuse_agent, medium — 'is there already a document/RAG pipeline ingesting these globs?' NO, and the answer is stronger than absence. rag_index takes its text from the ORCHESTRATION PAYLOAD (content_field out of collected_data, rag_actions.go:138-139) — it has no filepath.Glob, no Walk, no root, and cannot reach a repo file unless another step already read it in. Empirically the whole RAG surface is 34 rows in 2 collections with ZERO from repo markdown, against 4,992 code_symbols rows. And decisively: **rag_lookup is wired to exactly one agent, rag-test-agent.** No diagnostic or council seat can reach knowledge_base. The readers this plan serves — diagnose-agent, feature-designer, fix-proposer — reach code_symbols and nothing else, so ingesting markdown into the RAG surface would not make it findable by them AT ALL. This is not a second way to do the same thing; it is the only way that reaches the consumer.

(2) guardian, low — 'corroborate no-reader-switches-on-kind by naming which pipelines touch this table.' Four agent_definitions touch it, ONE writes: code-indexer writes (index_symbols); diagnose-agent reads (lookup_symbols); feature-designer and fix-proposer read (code_lookup). Seven live read sites enumerated in grounded_in with their column lists — NONE selects kind. The column reaches Go in exactly two places, both inside lookup_code_symbols, both handing it to scanCodeSymbolRows:566-585, which puts it in a result map and never compares it. **AND A CORRECTION I OWE THE COUNCIL: rounds 6-7 said the branch-on-kind grep returned 'one hit'. It returns FOUR** — diagnose_code_lookup_action.go:246, :415, :550 and code_symbols_actions.go:430. None is the column: the first three are the CODE_CHECK kind (symbol|content|ls), a different namespace, and the fourth is the analyser's typeDef.Kind on the write path. The conclusion is unchanged and the count I gave was wrong; guardian was right to refuse to take it on trust.

(3) guardian, low — 'confirm from the DB side that only one agent_definition wires IndexCodeSymbolsAction.' Confirmed, one row: code-indexer / index_symbols. Query and result in grounded_in.

(4) debug_historian, medium — 'the plan specifies no pod-binary verification anywhere; all VERIFY assertions are DB-only.' **This was a real gap and the diagnosis is sharper than the objection.** Every existing assertion would read IDENTICALLY against a pod that never received the code: kind='doc' rows would simply not appear, which is indistinguishable from 'the roll has not happened yet'. So VERIFY gains a step 0 that greps the RUNNING pod, and it is discriminating rather than decorative because the pre-roll baseline is MEASURED, not assumed: on agent-chassis-74dbd9c9f4-7p6d8 today, flattenMarkdown 0 / composeDocContent 0 / defaultDocGlobs 0, with composeSymbolContent 2 and scanCodeSymbolRows 2 as the positive control proving the grep instrument works on that binary.

(5) prior_art_librarian, low — 'the owning-pipeline claim has no grounded_in line, unlike every other factual claim.' Fair, and it was the only prose-only claim in the submission. Now a query result: scheduled_tasks row code-index-refresh / index-orchestrator / 86400s / enabled, last fired 2026-07-28 12:46:27Z.

(6) prior_art_librarian, low, explicitly informational — the site_work_items negative. Not load-bearing this round (the prune is untouched); it lives in bugs_open/135 where the prune fix will be made, and the schema check belongs to that bug, not this plan. Left uncited here deliberately rather than padding grounded_in with a fact this plan does not rest on.

ALSO CORRECTED, unprompted: grounded_in's last entry still carried '~1,749 total against 4,992' — the stale figure the rationale itself corrects to ~3,472. A submission that corrects a number in prose while leaving it in the evidence is exactly the drift this workstream reviews for. Fixed at source.

CARRIED FORWARD, unchanged and previously checked: docs/ is on disk (github_source.go:196-245 writes every tar entry, no path filter; the analyse_repo_local_action.go:285 exclude is analyser-time) and out.Root survives collected_data (07-04 layer-1 run logged root=/tmp/analyser-src-451921075 files_read=543); the register glob is register/*.md (110 entries), not the parent (28 superseded planning docs) — round 1's real defect; no markdown splitter exists to reuse (chunkContent is a fixed-width window, extractProductSection truncates at a marker list, goldmark is go.sum-graph-only and imported nowhere).

SIZING: ~3,472 sections against 4,992 code rows, +70%.

THE PRUNE remains out of scope and filed as bugs_open/135, unowned. Prune behaviour after this plan is exactly what it is today.

plan.summary: ROUND 7, SCOPE SPLIT. D11 layer 1b: relax the kind CHECK and index markdown sections from four durable prose sources into code_symbols, reusing layer 1's body column and content search. The prune-safety sub-feature that accreted across rounds 4-6 -- and which generated ALL of round 6's objections while the core drew none -- is removed and filed as bugs_open/135, because it guards a pre-existing exposure on the code rows independent of this change. Prune behaviour is unchanged from today.

edits.rationale: code_symbols.kind carries a CHECK permitting Go kinds ONLY, so a markdown row cannot be inserted at all -- the mechanical blocker. Verbatim from the live DB: CHECK ((kind = ANY (ARRAY['func'::text, 'method'::text, 'struct'::text, 'interface'::text, 'alias'::text, 'type'::text, 'var'::text, 'const'::text]))). Adds 'doc'. READERS enumerated for guardian, and RE-MEASURED IN ROUND 8 against its objection that this claim is one its own tier cannot verify (code_checks see declarations, never switch bodies): seven live read sites, NONE selecting kind; the column reaches Go only at code_symbols_actions.go:528 and :549, both -> scanCodeSymbolRows:566-585, which scans it into a result map and never compares it. Four branch sites on a variable NAMED kind exist and none is the column (three are the code_check kind namespace, one is the analyser's typeDef.Kind on the write path) -- ROUNDS 6-7 SAID 'ONE HIT' AND THAT COUNT WAS WRONG. Full census with column lists and file:line in grounded_in. NUMBER MOVES -- 253 is highest today, but this workstream's last migration was approved as 241 and shipped as 243 because two sessions took 241 and 242 inside four hours. Re-read the max immediately before writing the file.

ROUND 2, answering debug_historian (medium): the needle-gate discipline wants verify AND rollback as separate files, and this constraint relaxation is what makes the Go writer's INSERTs possible at all -- so a bad flattenMarkdown run had no scripted recovery. THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS FILE IS NOT TRIVIAL: the old CHECK cannot be restored while kind='doc' rows exist, so the rows must be deleted FIRST or the ALTER fails with a check-violation on existing data. Written as one transaction so a half-rollback is not representable.

ROUND 3, rewritten for bug_historian (medium): the round-2 guard fired only on a TOTAL of zero, and round 1's real defect was non-zero-but-wrong-source. Now: counts are tracked PER GLOB and returned; a glob matching ZERO FILES is a hard error (the plan's only fail-loud escalation, because a source contributing nothing is indistinguishable from a source that does not exist); and the scope/path-shape assertion runs HERE, every index, not only in a VERIFY a human runs once. NOT REUSING, with the search attached in the rationale: chunkContent (rag_actions.go:396) is a fixed-width window; extractProductSection (vet_med_price_scrape_action.go:650) is markdown- and heading-aware but TRUNCATES at a fixed end-marker list and returns one prefix with no spans; no markdown parser is a dependency (goldmark is go.sum-graph-only, absent from go.mod, imported nowhere). Suffix determinism, for guardian (low): the counter is a per-file map[string]int incremented during ONE top-to-bottom pass over the file's own lines, so the Nth occurrence gets the same suffix every run -- document order, never map iteration order.

content does THREE jobs -- trigram text, the EMBEDDED text, and the input to content_hash which is the re-embed trigger. composeSymbolContent keeps the code BODY out for exactly this reason; markdown must obey the same rule or the first reindex re-embeds all 4,992 existing rows plus the new ones. So content is heading + path only; the section text goes to body, which is what the content check now searches anyway.

ROUND 7: append markdown rows to the Go rows before the EXISTING upsert/prune loop, which is UNCHANGED by this plan. Round 4-6's prune floor is removed and filed as bugs_open/135 -- it guards a pre-existing exposure on the code rows that exists with or without this change, and iterating it here was spending council rounds on a different change. Prune behaviour after this plan is exactly what it is today. THE GLOBS ARE THE DESIGN and round 1 got one wrong: the register is register/*.md (110 entries), not the parent (28 superseded planning docs). Owning pipeline, NOW A QUERY RESULT rather than prose (prior_art_librarian + guardian, round 7 -- it was the only prose-only claim in the submission): agent_definitions holds EXACTLY ONE wiring of index_code_symbols, code-indexer/index_symbols, so single-pipeline ownership of the write path is settled from the DB side; scheduled_tasks holds code-index-refresh -> index-orchestrator, 86400s, enabled, last fired 2026-07-28 12:46:27Z. Both queries and both results in grounded_in.

ROUND 8, answering debug_historian (medium): this file's assertions were ALL DB-only, and that is a named gap on this platform, not a hypothetical one. The sharper form of the objection: every assertion below would read IDENTICALLY against a pod that never received the code -- kind='doc' rows would simply be absent, which is indistinguishable from 'the roll has not happened yet'. Step 0 closes that, and it is discriminating rather than decorative because the pre-roll baseline is MEASURED. A SUPPLEMENT, not a fix -- explicitly conceding editquality (low, edit 6): this file changes no behaviour and is not counted as covering any mechanism. It exists because 243's VERIFY caught a real defect in layer 1 that a reviewer had been asked to eyeball. Carries the 243 lesson forward: that file's EXPLAIN stayed pinned to the OLD predicate after the code changed, so it reported on a query nobody ran while presenting as coverage -- these assertions must be re-read whenever flattenMarkdown or the globs change.

plan.risks: (1) THE ONE INVARIANT: content and content_hash must not gain section text or every existing row re-embeds. composeDocContent is heading+path only; the VERIFY asserts hash integrity across ALL rows. (2) EMBEDDING COST: ~3,472 new rows each embed once on first index. Layer 1's cost was zero-by-construction; this is not, and it is stated. (3) IDENTITY COLLISION: in-file duplicate headings measured at 1 today (WRONG_CALLS.md 212 headings / 211 unique); the suffix counter runs in document order over one top-to-bottom pass, so it is stable across runs. (4) SCOPE IS THE DESIGN AND ROUND 1 GOT IT WRONG ONCE: the register glob pointed at 28 superseded planning docs instead of 110 register entries -- a wrong glob poisons the corpus with the stale-doc class this plan exists to keep out, while every counter reports success. Per-glob counts, a zero-match glob failing the doc half, and the VERIFY's out-of-scope + register_sections assertions are the guards. (5) BLAST RADIUS of the CHECK widening, enumerated and re-checked: no reader switches on kind; the only behavioural change is that a doc row can appear in lookup_code_symbols' top-k, which is the intended effect. (6) PRUNE: unchanged by this plan. The pre-existing no-floor exposure is bugs_open/135. (7) DEPLOY: Go is inert until the image rolls; the CHECK relaxes immediately and markdown simply does not arrive until then -- a degrade, not a break. HOW THE ROLL IS CONFIRMED (debug_historian, round 7 -- the plan previously said Go was inert but never said how it would know the roll happened): no doc_sections count is trusted until the RUNNING pod's binary greps non-zero for flattenMarkdown, read against the measured pre-roll baseline of 0 with composeSymbolContent=2 as the positive control. VERIFY step 0. Neither git nor the image tag is evidence.
